newsitem.title: ITALY: Turncoat says Sicilian Mafia cremated victims.
newsitem.headline: Turncoat says Sicilian Mafia cremated victims.

text.p: The Sicilian Mafia has used an incinerator set up in a Palermo mobster's backyard to cremate dozens of victims whom authorities have never found, a Mafia turncoat has told Italian police.

Police said that Francesco Onorato, a mobster convicted on numerous counts of homocide who has turned state's evidence, accused boss Salvatore Graziano of maintaining the incinerator in his garden in the Palermo district of Tommaso Natale.

Police in the Sicilian capital said that, among other victims, the incinerator had been used in 1989 to cremate the owner of a Palermo bird shop who had challenged the Mafia's monopoly on kidnapping and theft in his neighbourhood, according to Onorato.
The body of the shopkeeper, identified as Antonio Noto, was never found.
Onorato was among several turncoats whose testimony was being used in an investigation into the Mafia's virtual stranglehold over the ship-building industry in Palermo.
Palermo police arrested 15 people on Saturday in connection with the probe.
Police informed Graziano, who was already in jail, that his role in the case was being investigated.
Police in the southern mainland Calabria region said they had arrested fugitive gangster Girolamo Mole, one of Italy's most-wanted Mafia bosses.

The 36-year-old Mole, nicknammed "Mommo", was seized early on Saturday near the town of Gioia Tauro. He is considered a top boss of Calabria's 'Ndrangheta mafia and among Italy's 30 most-wanted criminals.
Mole had been on the run since June 1993 when the first of eight arrest warrants was issued against him on charges such as Mafia association, murder, extortion and other crimes.
An international arrest warrant had been issued against him in December 1995.
News of his arrest came after police said they had smashed a heroin ring in Reggio Calabria, arresting 50 people.
Saturday's events came after the government approved a plan on Friday to send 500 troops to Naples to help police crack down on gangsters who are plaguing the southern port with bloody turf wars.
